description: Westermo and research partners publish industrial communication traffic from a twelve-device test network running a bottle-filling factory simulation. The dataset contains about 1.8 million packets from roughly 90 minutes, with raw PCAP captures and processed CSV flows containing 50 features and four labels. Measurements come from several points in the network. Ninety-six events cover benign SSH, failed SSH attempts, address misconfiguration, duplicate addresses, port scans and man-in-the-middle activity. The GitHub README documents reduced and extended captures, topology and alternative event-labelling strategies. The data are freely available under CC BY 4.0. A limitation is duplicate packets because devices capture both incoming and outgoing traffic. Some traffic was removed for information-security reasons, and physical-world-simulator traffic is not representative of an actual factory. These are experimental traces, not evidence of the frequency of attacks in operating plants. A reviewer-assessed use is testing industrial-network anomaly models and traffic assumptions for platform-ns-3. Compatibility with that simulator was not tested.
